**High pressure building across southern England is driving trader consensus toward a peak of 32–33°C in London on July 29, with Met Office guidance indicating a maximum of 33°C under mostly sunny skies and light winds.** 

Recent model runs show warm southerly flow advecting air from the continent, supporting daytime highs several degrees above the July average of ~22–24°C, consistent with the ongoing warm spell across southeast England. Minor forecast spread arises from differences in predicted cloud cover timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the strength of the urban heat-island effect in central London, which can add 1–2°C locally. Official agencies such as the Met Office and ECMWF continue to converge on dry, stable conditions with little risk of significant cooling until later in the week, leaving the outcome sensitive to the final 24–48 hours of model updates. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 32–34°C band while assigning low odds to extremes below 30°C or above 35°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Marine layer and persistent onshore flow from the Pacific are the dominant factors capping San Francisco highs near or slightly above seasonal normals around 70°F on July 29. Official NWS guidance and model consensus point to a gradual warming trend midweek behind an expanding ridge, yet strong afternoon sea breezes and possible morning stratus should limit inland heat intrusion into the city. Recent Bay Area heat episodes have largely spared the immediate coast, keeping the distribution centered on 68–73°F bins. Key variables include marine-layer depth, wind speed and direction, and any late-day clearing that could allow an extra degree or two; traders price the highest uncertainty around these thresholds given typical July variability and the one-day forecast horizon.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus around 22–24°C for São Paulo’s July 30 high reflects ensemble model runs from GFS and ECMWF showing modest daytime warming under subtropical high pressure, with light winds and limited cloud cover allowing some solar heating during the Southern Hemisphere winter. Official forecasts from sources such as the Met Office currently indicate a peak near 20–21°C, consistent with July climatology of 22–24°C averages at the Guarulhos reference station, though urban heat-island effects and exact timing of maximum temperature introduce 1–2°C run-to-run variability. The tight spread across outcomes stems from these small differences in insolation, boundary-layer mixing, and potential for brief cloud increases, with new model updates expected to refine the range before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Short-term forecast uncertainty around the seasonal average drives the tight clustering of implied probabilities near 32–34°C for Kuala Lumpur’s July 31 daily maximum.** 

Kuala Lumpur’s southwest monsoon climatology typically produces afternoon highs of 31–33°C, with the urban heat island and high humidity pushing readings toward the upper end on clearer days. Recent model guidance and the July 27 outcome of exactly 33°C illustrate how modest differences in morning cloud cover, timing of convective showers, or boundary-layer mixing can shift the peak by 1–2°C. Strengthening El Niño conditions have raised the regional temperature baseline and reduced rainfall likelihood, tilting the distribution slightly above the long-term July mean of ~33°C, yet the market’s near-even split between 33°C (29.5%) and 34°C (27.5%) reflects residual uncertainty in the final 48-hour convective evolution. Official short-range updates from MetMalaysia and global ensembles will determine whether the peak settles in the lower or upper half of the narrow 32–34°C window.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LTFM

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-range forecasts from sources like BBC Weather and timeanddate indicate sunny conditions with a maximum of around 29°C expected for Istanbul on July 31, consistent with typical late-July patterns where daily highs average 27–29°C amid stable high pressure. Market-implied odds favoring 26°C (44%) and 27°C (22.5%) likely reflect trader focus on potential measurement at official stations, minor model variability in peak timing, or slight cooling influences such as northeasterly breezes, rather than broader regional projections. With resolution imminent, updated numerical weather prediction runs from agencies like the Turkish State Meteorological Service could refine these probabilities by confirming exact peak values against historical July baselines of 28–30°C.
